sanskrit: ṛṣibhiḥ saṃparityaktā dharmayuktā mahāvratāḥ drutam āgamya cocus tā devasenāpatiṃ prabhum
english: Abandoned by their sages, those virtuous women of great vows came swiftly and cried out to the lord, the commander of the divine host.

sanskrit: vayaṃ putra parityaktā bhartṛbhir devasaṃmitaiḥ akāraṇād ruṣā tāta puṇyasthānāt paricyutāḥ
english: "We, O son, have been abandoned by our husbands, equal to the gods, cast out from our sacred abodes without cause and in anger, dear child.

sanskrit: asmābhiḥ kila jātas tvam iti kenāpy udāhṛtam asatyam etat saṃśrutya tasmān nas trātum arhasi
english: Someone proclaimed that you were born of us — having heard this falsehood, our husbands deserted us. Therefore you ought to protect us.

sanskrit: akṣayaś ca bhavet svargas tvatprasādād dhi naḥ prabho tvāṃ putraṃ cāpy abhīpsāmaḥ kṛtvaitad anṛṇo bhava
english: Through your grace, O lord, heaven will be imperishable for us. We desire you as our son — having done this much, be free of debt to us."

sanskrit: skanda uvāca mātaro hi bhavatyo me suto vo 'ham aninditāḥ yac cābhīpsatha tat sarvaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati vas tathā
english: Skanda said: "You are indeed my mothers, O blameless ones, and I am your son. Whatever you desire shall come to pass for you."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam ukte tataḥ śakraṃ kiṃ kāryam iti so 'bravīt uktaḥ skandena brūhīti so 'bravīd vāsavas tataḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: When this was spoken, Skanda then asked Śakra: "What task remains?" Addressed by Skanda with "Speak!", Vāsava then replied.

sanskrit: abhijit spardhamānā tu rohiṇyā kanyasī svasā icchantī jyeṣṭhatāṃ devī tapas taptuṃ vanaṃ gatā
english: "Abhijit, the younger sister of Rohiṇī, competing with her and desiring precedence, has gone to the forest to practise austerities.

sanskrit: tatra mūḍho 'smi bhadraṃ te nakṣatraṃ gaganāc cyutam kālaṃ tv imaṃ paraṃ skanda brahmaṇā saha cintaya
english: In this matter I am bewildered — blessings upon you; the constellation has fallen from the sky. Reflect now upon this critical time together with Brahmā, O Skanda.

sanskrit: dhaniṣṭhādis tadā kālo brahmaṇā parinirmitaḥ rohiṇyādyo 'bhavat pūrvam evaṃ saṃkhyā samābhavat
english: The age ordained by Brahmā then began with Dhaniṣṭhā; previously it had begun with Rohiṇī — thus the count of the constellations was reckoned.

sanskrit: evam ukte tu śakreṇa tridivaṃ kṛttikā gatāḥ nakṣatraṃ śakaṭākāraṃ bhāti tad vahnidaivatam
english: When this was said by Śakra, the Kṛttikās went up to heaven; that constellation, shaped like a cart, shines forth — it has Fire as its deity.

sanskrit: vinatā cābravīt skandaṃ mama tvaṃ piṇḍadaḥ sutaḥ icchāmi nityam evāhaṃ tvayā putra sahāsitum
english: And Vinatā spoke to Skanda: "You are my son who offers me funerary cakes. I always wish to dwell with you, O son."

sanskrit: skanda uvāca evam astu namas te 'stu putrasnehāt praśādhi mām snuṣayā pūjyamānā vai devi vatsyasi nityadā
english: Skanda said: "So be it — homage to you. Out of a mother's affection, command me. Worshipped by your daughter-in-law, O goddess, you shall dwell here always."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca atha mātṛgaṇaḥ sarvaḥ skandaṃ vacanam abravīt vayaṃ sarvasya lokasya mātaraḥ kavibhiḥ stutāḥ icchāmo mātaras tubhyaṃ bhavituṃ pūjayasva naḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then the entire assembly of mothers spoke this word to Skanda: "We are the mothers of all the worlds, praised by the wise. We wish to be mothers to you — worship us."

sanskrit: skanda uvāca mātaras tu bhavatyo me bhavatīnām ahaṃ sutaḥ ucyatāṃ yan mayā kāryaṃ bhavatīnām athepsitam
english: Skanda said: "You are indeed my mothers, and I am the son of you all. Tell me what should be done by me, and what is desired by you."

sanskrit: mātara ūcuḥ yās tu tā mātaraḥ pūrvaṃ lokasyāsya prakalpitāḥ asmākaṃ tad bhavet sthānaṃ tāsāṃ caiva na tad bhavet
english: The mothers said: "Those who were formerly ordained as the mothers of this world — that position should be ours, and not theirs.

sanskrit: bhavema pūjyā lokasya na tāḥ pūjyāḥ surarṣabha prajāsmākaṃ hṛtās tābhis tvatkṛte tāḥ prayaccha naḥ
english: We should be the ones worshipped by the world, not they, O bull among gods. Our progeny were taken away by them for your sake — give those children back to us."

sanskrit: skanda uvāca dattāḥ prajā na tāḥ śakyā bhavatībhir niṣevitum anyāṃ vaḥ kāṃ prayacchāmi prajāṃ yāṃ manasecchatha
english: Skanda said: "The progeny that were given cannot be reclaimed by you. What other progeny shall I grant you — tell me what you desire in your hearts."

sanskrit: mātara ūcuḥ icchāma tāsāṃ mātṝṇāṃ prajā bhoktuṃ prayaccha naḥ tvayā saha pṛthagbhūtā ye ca tāsām atheśvarāḥ
english: The mothers said: "We wish to feed upon the progeny of those other mothers — grant us this. Also those lords who have separated themselves from them along with you."

sanskrit: skanda uvāca prajā vo dadmi kaṣṭaṃ tu bhavatībhir udāhṛtam parirakṣata bhadraṃ vaḥ prajāḥ sādhu namaskṛtāḥ
english: Skanda said: "I grant you progeny — but what you have said is harsh. Protect the children well — blessings upon you! Those who are duly honoured will be well."

sanskrit: mātara ūcuḥ parirakṣāma bhadraṃ te prajāḥ skanda yathecchasi tvayā no rocate skanda sahavāsaś ciraṃ prabho
english: The mothers said: "We shall protect the children as you wish, blessings to you, O Skanda. We desire to dwell long together with you, O lord."

sanskrit: skanda uvāca yāvat ṣoḍaśa varṣāṇi bhavanti taruṇāḥ prajāḥ prabādhata manuṣyāṇāṃ tāvad rūpaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ
english: Skanda said: "For as long as children are young, up to the age of sixteen years, afflict the progeny of humans with your various forms.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca vaḥ pradāsyāmi raudram ātmānam avyayam paramaṃ tena sahitā sukhaṃ vatsyatha pūjitāḥ
english: And I shall bestow upon you my terrible and imperishable supreme self. Together with that, you shall dwell in happiness, honoured by all."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ śarīrāt skandasya puruṣaḥ kāñcanaprabhaḥ bhoktuṃ prajāḥ sa martyānāṃ niṣpapāta mahābalaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then from the body of Skanda there sprang forth a great-armed being radiant as gold, mighty in strength, to feed upon the progeny of mortals.

sanskrit: apatat sa tadā bhūmau visaṃjño 'tha kṣudhānvitaḥ skandena so 'bhyanujñāto raudrarūpo 'bhavad grahaḥ skandāpasmāram ity āhur grahaṃ taṃ dvijasattamāḥ
english: He fell then to the ground, senseless and tormented by hunger; authorized by Skanda, he became a terrible-formed planetary spirit. The best of twice-born call that spirit Skanda-apasmāra.

sanskrit: vinatā tu mahāraudrā kathyate śakunigrahaḥ pūtanāṃ rākṣasīṃ prāhus taṃ vidyāt pūtanāgraham
english: Vinatā of terrifying form is known as the Śakuni-graha; they call Pūtanā a rākṣasī — one should know her as the Pūtanā-graha.

sanskrit: kaṣṭā dāruṇarūpeṇa ghorarūpā niśācarī piśācī dāruṇākārā kathyate śītapūtanā garbhān sā mānuṣīṇāṃ tu harate ghoradarśanā
english: Terrible with a dreadful form, a hideous night-roamer, a piśācī of frightful shape — she is called Śīta-pūtanā; of fearsome appearance, she steals the wombs of human women.

sanskrit: aditiṃ revatīṃ prāhur grahas tasyās tu raivataḥ so 'pi bālāñ śiśūn ghoro bādhate vai mahāgrahaḥ
english: They call Aditi the Revatī; the planetary spirit belonging to her is Raivata. That great terrible graha also afflicts young infants.

sanskrit: daityānāṃ yā ditir mātā tām āhur mukhamaṇḍikām atyarthaṃ śiśumāṃsena saṃprahṛṣṭā durāsadā
english: Diti, who is the mother of the daityas — they call her Mukha-maṇḍikā, exceedingly delighted by the flesh of infants, impossible to overcome.

sanskrit: kumārāś ca kumāryaś ca ye proktāḥ skandasaṃbhavāḥ te 'pi garbhabhujaḥ sarve kauravya sumahāgrahāḥ
english: And those youths and maidens who are said to have arisen from Skanda — they too are eaters of the womb, O Kauravya, all of them very great planetary spirits.

sanskrit: tāsām eva kumārīṇāṃ patayas te prakīrtitāḥ ajñāyamānā gṛhṇanti bālakān raudrakarmiṇaḥ
english: The husbands of those very maidens are proclaimed as well; acting unrecognized, those doers of terrible deeds seize children.

sanskrit: gavāṃ mātā tu yā prājñaiḥ kathyate surabhir nṛpa śakunis tām athāruhya saha bhuṅkte śiśūn bhuvi
english: She who is known by the wise as Surabhi, the mother of cows, O king — Śakuni mounts her and feeds upon infants upon the earth alongside her.

sanskrit: saramā nāma yā mātā śunāṃ devī janādhipa sāpi garbhān samādatte mānuṣīṇāṃ sadaiva hi
english: She who is called Saramā, the divine mother of dogs, O lord of the people — she too perpetually takes the wombs of human women.

sanskrit: pādapānāṃ ca yā mātā karañjanilayā hi sā karañje tāṃ namasyanti tasmāt putrārthino narāḥ
english: And she who is the mother of trees, dwelling in the karañja tree — men who desire sons therefore worship her in the karañja.

sanskrit: ime tv aṣṭādaśānye vai grahā māṃsamadhupriyāḥ dvipañcarātraṃ tiṣṭhanti satataṃ sūtikāgṛhe
english: These eighteen others among the grahas, lovers of flesh and honey, remain for twice five nights continually in the lying-in chamber.

sanskrit: kadrūḥ sūkṣmavapur bhūtvā garbhiṇīṃ praviśed yadā bhuṅkte sā tatra taṃ garbhaṃ sā tu nāgaṃ prasūyate
english: When Kadrū, assuming a subtle form, enters a pregnant woman, she feeds upon that womb within; and the woman then gives birth to a serpent.

sanskrit: gandharvāṇāṃ tu yā mātā sā garbhaṃ gṛhya gacchati tato vilīnagarbhā sā mānuṣī bhuvi dṛśyate
english: The mother of the Gandharvas seizes the womb and departs; that human woman is then seen upon the earth with her womb dissolved.

sanskrit: yā janitrī tv apsarasāṃ garbham āste pragṛhya sā upaviṣṭaṃ tato garbhaṃ kathayanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: She who is the mother of the Apsarasas sits within after seizing the womb; the wise then call that pregnancy a seated or dormant one.

sanskrit: lohitasyodadheḥ kanyā dhātrī skandasya sā smṛtā lohitāyanir ity evaṃ kadambe sā hi pūjyate
english: The daughter of the red ocean is remembered as the nurse of Skanda; known as Lohitāyanī, she is worshipped in the kadamba tree.

sanskrit: puruṣeṣu yathā rudras tathāryā pramadāsv api āryā mātā kumārasya pṛthakkāmārtham ijyate
english: As Rudra is among men, so is Āryā among women. Āryā, the mother of the Kumāra, is separately propitiated for the fulfilment of desires.

sanskrit: evam ete kumārāṇāṃ mayā proktā mahāgrahāḥ yāvat ṣoḍaśa varṣāṇi aśivās te śivās tataḥ
english: Thus have I described these great planetary spirits of children. Up to the age of sixteen years they are inauspicious; thereafter they become auspicious.

sanskrit: ye ca mātṛgaṇāḥ proktāḥ puruṣāś caiva ye grahāḥ sarve skandagrahā nāma jñeyā nityaṃ śarīribhiḥ
english: The assemblies of mothers that have been described, and also the grahas who are persons — all of these are to be known always by embodied beings as the Skanda-grahas.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ praśamanaṃ kāryaṃ snānaṃ dhūpam athāñjanam balikarmopahāraś ca skandasyejyā viśeṣataḥ
english: For their pacification, one should perform bathing, fumigation, and anointing; offering of bali and gifts; and in particular the worship of Skanda.

sanskrit: evam ete 'rcitāḥ sarve prayacchanti śubhaṃ nṛṇām āyur vīryaṃ ca rājendra samyak pūjānamaskṛtāḥ
english: When all of these are thus worshipped and saluted with proper veneration, O king of kings, they bestow auspiciousness, long life, and vigour upon men.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ tu ṣoḍaśād varṣād ye bhavanti grahā nṛṇām tān ahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi namaskṛtya maheśvaram
english: Now I shall declare, after bowing to Maheśvara, those planetary spirits that afflict men beyond the age of sixteen years.

sanskrit: yaḥ paśyati naro devāñ jāgrad vā śayito 'pi vā unmādyati sa tu kṣipraṃ taṃ tu devagrahaṃ viduḥ
english: A man who sees the gods, whether waking or lying down, quickly falls into madness — him they know as seized by the Deva-graha.

sanskrit: āsīnaś ca śayānaś ca yaḥ paśyati naraḥ pitṝn unmādyati sa tu kṣipraṃ sa jñeyas tu pitṛgrahaḥ
english: A man who sees the ancestors while sitting or lying down quickly becomes mad — he is to be known as seized by the Pitṛ-graha.

sanskrit: avamanyati yaḥ siddhān kruddhāś cāpi śapanti yam unmādyati sa tu kṣipraṃ jñeyaḥ siddhagrahas tu saḥ
english: One who scorns the Siddhas, and whom those angered Siddhas curse, quickly goes mad — he is to be known as seized by the Siddha-graha.

sanskrit: upāghrāti ca yo gandhān rasāṃś cāpi pṛthagvidhān unmādyati sa tu kṣipraṃ sa jñeyo rākṣaso grahaḥ
english: One who smells odours and tastes of various kinds not present to others and quickly goes mad — he is to be known as seized by the Rākṣasa-graha.

sanskrit: gandharvāś cāpi yaṃ divyāḥ saṃspṛśanti naraṃ bhuvi unmādyati sa tu kṣipraṃ graho gāndharva eva saḥ
english: When the divine Gandharvas touch a man on earth and he quickly goes mad — that planetary seizure is indeed the Gāndharva-graha.

sanskrit: āviśanti ca yaṃ yakṣāḥ puruṣaṃ kālaparyaye unmādyati sa tu kṣipraṃ jñeyo yakṣagrahas tu saḥ
english: When Yakṣas enter a man at a turn of time and he quickly goes mad — he is to be known as seized by the Yakṣa-graha.

sanskrit: adhirohanti yaṃ nityaṃ piśācāḥ puruṣaṃ kva cit unmādyati sa tu kṣipraṃ paiśācaṃ taṃ grahaṃ viduḥ
english: When Piśācas continually mount a man in some place and he quickly goes mad — they know that planetary seizure as the Paiśāca-graha.

sanskrit: yasya doṣaiḥ prakupitaṃ cittaṃ muhyati dehinaḥ unmādyati sa tu kṣipraṃ sādhanaṃ tasya śāstrataḥ
english: When by one's own faults the mind of an embodied being is disturbed and bewildered, and he quickly becomes mad — his remedy is prescribed by the scriptures.

sanskrit: vaiklavyāc ca bhayāc caiva ghorāṇāṃ cāpi darśanāt unmādyati sa tu kṣipraṃ sattvaṃ tasya tu sādhanam
english: When from weakness of spirit, fear, or the sight of terrible things a man quickly becomes mad — for him strength of character is the remedy.

sanskrit: kaś cit krīḍitukāmo vai bhoktukāmas tathāparaḥ abhikāmas tathaivānya ity eṣa trividho grahaḥ
english: Some are desirous of sport, another desires to eat, another is filled with desire — thus this planetary seizure is of three kinds.

sanskrit: yāvat saptativarṣāṇi bhavanty ete grahā nṛṇām ataḥ paraṃ dehināṃ tu grahatulyo bhavej jvaraḥ
english: These grahas afflict men for up to seventy years; beyond that age, for embodied beings, fever acts like a planetary seizure.

sanskrit: aprakīrṇendriyaṃ dāntaṃ śuciṃ nityam atandritam āstikaṃ śraddadhānaṃ ca varjayanti sadā grahāḥ
english: The grahas always shun a man whose senses are not scattered, who is self-controlled, pure, ever-vigilant, who believes in the scriptures, and who has faith.

sanskrit: ity eṣa te grahoddeśo mānuṣāṇāṃ prakīrtitaḥ na spṛśanti grahā bhaktān narān devaṃ maheśvaram
english: Thus this account of the grahas as they afflict humans has been set forth. The grahas do not touch those men who are devoted to the god Maheśvara.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca yadā skandena mātṝṇām evam etat priyaṃ kṛtam athainam abravīt svāhā mama putras tvam aurasaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: When Skanda had thus done this favour for the mothers, Svāhā then spoke to him: "You are my own begotten son."

sanskrit: icchāmy ahaṃ tvayā dattāṃ prītiṃ paramadurlabhām tām abravīt tataḥ skandaḥ prītim icchasi kīdṛśīm
english: "I desire a gift of joy from you, most difficult to obtain." Skanda then asked her: "What kind of joy do you wish?"

sanskrit: svāhovāca dakṣasyāhaṃ priyā kanyā svāhā nāma mahābhuja bālyāt prabhṛti nityaṃ ca jātakāmā hutāśane
english: Svāhā said: "I am the beloved daughter of Dakṣa, named Svāhā, O mighty-armed one. From childhood I have been perpetually enamoured of Hutāśana, the god of fire.

sanskrit: na ca māṃ kāminīṃ putra samyag jānāti pāvakaḥ icchāmi śāśvataṃ vāsaṃ vastuṃ putra sahāgninā
english: But Pāvaka does not truly know me, though I long for him, O son. I wish to dwell always with Agni, O son."

sanskrit: skanda uvāca havyaṃ kavyaṃ ca yat kiṃ cid dvijā mantrapuraskṛtam hoṣyanty agnau sadā devi svāhety uktvā samudyatam
english: Skanda said: "Whatever oblation — whether for the gods or for the ancestors — the twice-born, preceded by mantras, offer into fire, O goddess, shall always be offered with the utterance of the word 'Svāhā' as they prepare it.

sanskrit: adya prabhṛti dāsyanti suvṛttāḥ satpathe sthitāḥ evam agnis tvayā sārdhaṃ sadā vatsyati śobhane
english: From this day forward, the virtuous who walk the right path shall make this offering. Thus shall Agni always dwell with you, O beautiful one."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam uktā tataḥ svāhā tuṣṭā skandena pūjitā pāvakena samāyuktā bhartrā skandam apūjayat
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Thus addressed, Svāhā was satisfied, honoured by Skanda. Joined with Pāvaka, her husband, she in turn worshipped Skanda.

sanskrit: tato brahmā mahāsenaṃ prajāpatir athābravīt abhigaccha mahādevaṃ pitaraṃ tripurārdanam
english: Then Brahmā, the lord of creatures, spoke to Mahāsena: "Go to Mahādeva, your father, the destroyer of Tripura.

sanskrit: rudreṇāgniṃ samāviśya svāhām āviśya comayā hitārthaṃ sarvalokānāṃ jātas tvam aparājitaḥ
english: By Rudra entering into Agni and entering into Svāhā along with Umā, for the benefit of all the worlds you were born, O unconquered one.

sanskrit: umāyonyāṃ ca rudreṇa śukraṃ siktaṃ mahātmanā āste girau nipatitaṃ miñjikāmiñjikaṃ yataḥ
english: And the semen shed by the great-souled Rudra in Umā's womb fell upon the mountain and from it arose the pair called Miñjikā-miñjika.

sanskrit: saṃbhūtaṃ lohitode tu śukraśeṣam avāpatat sūryaraśmiṣu cāpy anyad anyac caivāpatad bhuvi āsaktam anyad vṛkṣeṣu tad evaṃ pañcadhāpatat
english: What arose fell into the red lake as the residue of the semen; another part fell in the rays of the sun, another fell upon the earth, another adhered to trees — thus it fell in five ways.

sanskrit: ta ete vividhākārā gaṇā jñeyā manīṣibhiḥ tava pāriṣadā ghorā ya ete piśitāśanāḥ
english: These hosts of various forms are to be known by the wise as your terrible attendants — these flesh-eaters who form your retinue.

sanskrit: evam astv iti cāpy uktvā mahāseno maheśvaram apūjayad ameyātmā pitaraṃ pitṛvatsalaḥ
english: Saying "so be it," Mahāsena, of immeasurable spirit, worshipped Maheśvara, his father, with a son's deep affection.

sanskrit: arkapuṣpais tu te pañca gaṇāḥ pūjyā dhanārthibhiḥ vyādhipraśamanārthaṃ ca teṣāṃ pūjāṃ samācaret
english: Those five hosts should be worshipped with arka flowers by those who desire wealth; and for the removal of disease, one should perform their worship.

sanskrit: miñjikāmiñjikaṃ caiva mithunaṃ rudrasaṃbhavam namaskāryaṃ sadaiveha bālānāṃ hitam icchatā
english: The couple Miñjikā-miñjika, born of Rudra, should always be reverently saluted here by one who wishes well for children.

sanskrit: striyo mānuṣamāṃsādā vṛddhikā nāma nāmataḥ vṛkṣeṣu jātās tā devyo namaskāryāḥ prajārthibhiḥ
english: The women-spirits who eat human flesh, called by the name Vṛddhikā, born in trees — those goddesses should be saluted by those who desire offspring.

sanskrit: evam ete piśācānām asaṃkhyeyā gaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ ghaṇṭāyāḥ sapatākāyāḥ śṛṇu me saṃbhavaṃ nṛpa
english: Thus these innumerable hosts of piśācas have been recounted. Now hear from me the origin of the bell together with the banner, O king.

sanskrit: airāvatasya ghaṇṭe dve vaijayantyāv iti śrute guhasya te svayaṃ datte śakreṇānāyya dhīmatā
english: Two bells of Airāvata, known as the Vaijayantyau, were brought by the wise Śakra and given by him personally to Guha.

sanskrit: ekā tatra viśākhasya ghaṇṭā skandasya cāparā patākā kārttikeyasya viśākhasya ca lohitā
english: Of those, one bell belongs to Viśākha and the other to Skanda. The banner is Kārttikeya's, and the red one belongs to Viśākha.

sanskrit: yāni krīḍanakāny asya devair dattāni vai tadā tair eva ramate devo mahāseno mahābalaḥ
english: The playthings that were given to him at that time by the gods — with those very things the mighty god Mahāsena delights himself.

sanskrit: sa saṃvṛtaḥ piśācānāṃ gaṇair devagaṇais tathā śuśubhe kāñcane śaile dīpyamānaḥ śriyā vṛtaḥ
english: Surrounded by hosts of piśācas and likewise by hosts of gods, blazing and encircled by glory, he shone upon the golden mountain.

sanskrit: tena vīreṇa śuśubhe sa śailaḥ śubhakānanaḥ ādityenevāṃśumatā mandaraś cārukandaraḥ
english: With that hero upon it, the mountain with its beautiful forests was resplendent — as Mandara with its lovely caverns shines with the radiant sun.

sanskrit: saṃtānakavanaiḥ phullaiḥ karavīravanair api pārijātavanaiś caiva japāśokavanais tathā
english: With groves of blossoming Santānaka trees, with forests of Karavīra, with groves of Pārijāta, with forests of Japā and Aśoka —
